title: cross-account-metrics-and-traces-forwarding-playbook-2025
author: Claire Nguyen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook documents an operational, secure approach for forwarding customer metrics and traces from a customer-managed AWS/GCP/Azure account into Redwood Console and an optional third-party observability backend (e.g., Splunk, Datadog, New Relic). It is intended for partners and enterprise customers who require cross-account telemetry collection without sending sensitive request payloads.

When to use this playbook:
- Customer has dedicated networking (VPC peering, PrivateLink, or firewall rules) and wants telemetry consolidated into Redwood Console.
- Customer requires audit-friendly cross-account forwarding with minimal footprint in customer environment.
- You need SRE-grade telemetry for QBRs, incident triage, and cost attribution.

Ownership and intent:
- Primary owner: Customer Success (onboarding team)
- Secondary owners: Eng-Infra (networking), Eng-SRE (alerting), Security (data handling)
- Goal: Reduce time-to-first-metric to < 4 hours for standard integrations; ensure data classification and retention meet customer SLA.

Prerequisites

Customer-side prerequisites:
1) Cloud account with the ability to deploy a small compute resource (Lambda/Cloud Run/VM) or install an agent on a telemetry gateway.
2) Network connectivity: one of the following: PrivateLink / VPC peering / IP allowlist for a Forwarder endpoint.
3) IAM/service account with least-privilege permissions to read metrics/traces and write to the forwarder resource.
4) List of metric namespaces and trace spans to be forwarded (sample set for initial onboarding).

Redwood-side prerequisites:
- Dedicated ingest endpoint (hosted) or customer-dedicated forwarder container image (for air-gapped/private deployments).
- Ingest API key scoped to metrics/traces ingest only. TTL and rotation policy to be agreed.

Architecture and flow

High-level flow (text diagram):
Customer telemetry source (Prometheus/OTel collector / vendor agent) --> Local forwarder (lightweight proxy) --> Cross-account secure tunnel / PrivateLink --> Redwood ingest endpoint --> Redwood Console (metrics store + traces index)

Security and data handling notes:
- Redact request-level payloads: Forward only metric names, numeric values, trace IDs, and safe tags. Customer must provide a redaction policy.
- TLS enforced mTLS where possible; fallback to TLS with mutual certificate pinning only if required by customer.
- KMS/HSM: For Private deployments, use customer-managed CMK to encrypt telemetry-at-rest.

Configuration reference (example table)

| Component | Minimum config (example) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OTel collector | receivers: prometheus, exporters: otlp | Set resource.attributes.service to customer service name |
| Local forwarder | image: rdwd/telemetry-forwarder:1.3.0\nargs: --mode=proxy --dest=https://ingest.rdwd.internal:443 | Supports batching, backoff, and delta compression |
| Ingest endpoint | api_key: redwood-ingest-<customer>-2025\nrate_limit: 5000 metrics/s | Scales by reserved capacity on Dedicated customers |
\nStep-by-step integration (typical onboarding)

1) Discovery (Customer Success + Solutions Engineer)
   - Collect account IDs, preferred connectivity pattern, sample metric namespaces, and SPIFF for sensitive fields.
   - Confirm retention and PII policy (default: 90 days for metrics, 30 days for traces unless enterprise package purchased).

2) Provisioning (Infra/Solutions)
   - Create ingest-scoped API key in Redwood Console and send to customer via secure channel (1Password/secure email).
   - Provide container image and Helm/K8s manifest or Lambda snippet. Example Lambda (Node):

   ```javascript
   const https = require('https');
   exports.handler = async (event) => {
     // minimal forwarder example
     const payload = JSON.stringify(event);
     const req = https.request(process.env.INGEST_URL, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.INGEST_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }, res=>{});
     req.write(payload); req.end();
     return { status: 'forwarded' };
   };
   ```

3) Network setup
   - If PrivateLink: exchange service names and create VPC endpoint in customer account. Validate DNS and route tables.
   - If IP allowlist: provide list of Redwood egress IP ranges and validate with customer firewall.

4) Deployment and smoke test
   - Deploy forwarder with a conservative batch interval (e.g., 10s) and start with 1% sample rate for traces.
   - Verify connectivity and ingest using the test pipe: POST /v1/ingest/health with api key. Expected response 200 and JSON with ingest_ack:true.

5) Validation and ramp
   - Confirm metric counts, label cardinality, and top-10 costly metrics. Tune sampling for traces and scale forwarder CPU/memory.
   - Enable dashboard template in Redwood Console and add to customer team workspace for QBR reporting.

Operational runbook (SRE-focused)

Alert triggers (suggestions):
- Forwarder down > 5m: SEV-2
- Ingest 5xxs > 1% over 15m: SEV-2
- Cardinality spike > 3x baseline over 30m: SEV-3
- Ingest lag > 2x expected: SEV-2

Runbook steps for Forwarder down:
1) Confirm forwarder compute is reachable (SSH/Cloud logs).
2) Check forwarder logs for connectivity errors, auth failures, or OOM.
3) If auth failure: rotate API key and redeploy.
4) If network issue: validate PrivateLink/VPC peering status and security group rules.
5) Escalate to Redwood Eng-SRE if unresolved after 30 minutes.

Cost and cardinality controls

To protect customer and Redwood unit economics, apply the following safeguards:
- Default label whitelist: service, env, region, customer_id. All other labels blocked unless approved.
- Default max_series_per_minute: 50k (can be raised on Dedicated contracts).
- Auto-sampling rule: When series growth > 2x, apply 10% sampling to trace spans and alert customer.

Troubleshooting matrix (common issues)

1) No metrics visible in Console
   - Check forwarder logs for 401/403 (bad api key).
   - Validate network route: traceroute to ingest endpoint from customer network.
   - Confirm Prometheus scrape job status and local collector metrics.

2) High 5xxs from ingest
   - Check payload size (max 1MB per batch).
   - Verify forwarder version compatibility (upgrade to rdwd/telemetry-forwarder:1.3.0+).
   - Check rate limits: backoff settings in forwarder should respect Retry-After header.

3) Exploding cardinality after deploy
   - Identify newly introduced labels with high cardinality via /v1/metrics/cardinality API.
   - Apply drop_labels rule in OTel collector and redeploy.

QBR and health metrics (what to report)

For customer QBRs, include: 
- Key metrics ingested per day (time series count)
- P95 latency for ingest (ms)
- Trace sampling rate and traced requests/day
- Alert volume and MTTR for telemetry-related incidents
- Cost delta attributable to telemetry (tokens/metrics cost)

Suggested dashboard tiles for QBR:
- "Telemetry Ingest Overview": daily metrics/time series, error rates
- "Top Label Cardinality": top 20 labels by series growth
- "Trace Coverage": % requests traced per service

Compliance and data retention

- Default retention: metrics 90 days, traces 30 days. Extended retention available under enterprise contract.
- PII handling: Do not forward request bodies, headers with auth tokens, or any field classified as "sensitive" by the customer redaction policy.
- Audit trail: All API key rotations and configuration changes are recorded and available in Redwood Console audit logs.

Escalation and support contact matrix

- Customer Success Oncall (first 30 minutes): cs-oncall@redwood.ai
- Eng-SRE escalation (30–120 minutes): sre-escalation@redwood.ai
- Security escalation (data leak suspected): sec-incident@redwood.ai (phone pager)

Appendix: example OTel snippet (prometheus scrape + exporter)

```yaml
receivers:
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
        - job_name: 'app'
          static_configs:
            - targets: ['localhost:9100']
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: '${INGEST_URL}'
    headers:
      'Authorization': 'Bearer ${INGEST_API_KEY}'
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [prometheus]
      exporters: [otlp]
```
